why it exists

At Initech our job queue accepted everything, and the database paid for it: every spike became a backlog, every backlog a page at 3 a.m. Retries made it worse.

what I did

I wrote it on weekends, then at work: a queue that measures how long the database takes to answer and stops taking jobs before it drowns. Producers get a clear "not now" with a retry time instead of a timeout.

what it changed

Five years and 290 forks later it runs in front of Postgres at companies of every size. At Globex it took queue incidents from eleven a quarter to none.
